situations.title: Acute chest pain
situations.priority: Second most common ED reason for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.

layer0.label: Complaint
layer0.detail: Pain, pressure, tightness or discomfort in the chest, shoulders, arms, neck, back, upper abdomen or jaw; shortness of breath and fatigue count as equivalents.

layer0.label: History
layer0.detail: Pain characteristics, accompanying symptoms and cardiac risk factors.

layer0.label: Vitals and exam
layer0.detail: Sweating and fast breathing lean toward ACS, fast heart rate and dyspnea toward PE, air under the skin toward esophageal rupture; chest wall tenderness or pain on inspiration leans noncardiac.

layer0.label: 12-lead ECG
layer0.detail: Recorded and read within 10 minutes of arrival.

gate.label: Unstable or ECG emergency
gate.detail: Ongoing ischemic discomfort, dynamic ECG change, hemodynamic instability or serious arrhythmia: emergency escalation.

gate.label: Stable, ECG non-diagnostic
gate.detail: Work through the hypotheses, must-not-miss first, with serial high-sensitivity troponin.

situations.gate_note: One normal ECG or one early troponin does not rule out ACS; patient characteristics must not be used to dismiss the complaint.

hypotheses.name: Aortic dissection
hypotheses.clue: Abrupt, tearing pain; pulse or BP differential

hypotheses.name: Common noncardiac causes
hypotheses.clue: Chest wall tenderness, pain on inspiration

steps.title: Focused history and exam
steps.description: Sets pre-test probability and picks the hypotheses to chase.

acs.text: Sweating and fast breathing raise suspicion.

pe.text: Fast heart rate and dyspnea raise suspicion.

ad.text: Abrupt, severe or tearing pain, pulse or BP differential, perfusion deficit.

ptx.text: Dyspnea, pain on inspiration, absent breath sounds on one side.

pna.text: Fever, localized pleuritic pain, dullness to percussion.

pc.text: Pleuritic, positional pain easing when leaning forward; friction rub.

nc.text: Chest wall tenderness or pain on inspiration points here.

steps.title: 12-lead ECG
steps.description: Best initial test; triggers the emergency pathway when ischemic.

acs.text: Ischemic or dynamic change escalates; one normal ECG does not rule ACS out.

pc.text: New widespread ST elevation or PR depression counts toward the two-of-four criteria.

steps.title: Chest radiograph
steps.description: Class 1 recommendation to look for other cardiac, pulmonary and thoracic causes.

ptx.text: Normal film with distress, pleuritic pain and hypoxia excludes it; absent vascular markings is diagnostic.

pna.text: Infiltrate or consolidation confirms; a normal film makes it unlikely.

pe.text: Often normal; with other causes excluded, a normal film raises PE probability.

ad.text: Mediastinal widening helps, but a film cannot rule out aortic syndromes at low probability.

pc.text: Recommended but does not establish the diagnosis.

steps.title: Serial high-sensitivity troponin and risk class
steps.description: Feeds the clinical decision pathway (low, intermediate, high risk).

acs.text: Low-risk class with non-ischemic ECG and negative serial troponin: no further acute testing.

pc.text: Recommended in suspected pericarditis but not diagnostic.

steps.title: Pre-test scoring of what is left
steps.timing: In parallel, for open must-not-miss causes
steps.description: A validated score sets the probability band that selects the next test.

pe.text: Wells two-level score; PERC first if suspicion is very low.

ad.text: ADD-RS 0 to 3: above 1 goes straight to imaging, 1 or less to D-dimer.

evidence.text: PE incidence is about 12% in the Wells unlikely band and about 37% in the likely band.
About 95% of patients with acute aortic dissection score intermediate or high on ADD-RS.
Meta-analysis: ADD-RS of 1 or more is about 94% sensitive alone and close to 100% with D-dimer; the best threshold depends on setting.

steps.title: D-dimer
steps.timing: Only at low or intermediate probability
steps.description: Rule-out blood test; never confirms.

pe.text: Wells 4 or less and D-dimer below the age-adjusted cutoff.

ad.text: ADD-RS 1 or less and D-dimer below 500 ng/mL (FEU): consider stopping; not externally validated.

steps.title: Definitive imaging for what remains
steps.description: Settles what earlier steps could not.

pe.text: CT pulmonary angiography: positive confirms, negative excludes.

ad.text: ECG-gated contrast CT from neck to pelvis is the recommended first-line imaging.

pc.text: Echocardiography: new or worsening effusion counts toward criteria.

evidence.text: ESC 2024 recommends a multiparametric diagnostic algorithm using ADD-RS (class I, level B).

steps.title: If the dangerous causes are eliminated
steps.description: Noncardiac causes become the working diagnosis.

nc.text: Chest wall pain, reflux esophagitis and costochondritis are most common in primary care.

acs.text: Low-risk patients do not need urgent stress testing or imaging.

eliminate_when.text: Low-risk class on the clinical decision pathway: non-ischemic ECG and negative serial high-sensitivity troponin.
Low-risk patients gain nothing from stress testing or imaging within 30 days.

do_not_rely.text: One normal ECG or one early troponin.
The chest radiograph.
Dismissing the complaint because of sex, age, race, language or anxiety history.
Assuming acute troponin is available everywhere.

pe.validation: Secondary summaries of ESC and NICE; verify against originals.

eliminate_when.text: Very low suspicion and all eight PERC criteria met.
Wells 4 or less and D-dimer below the age-adjusted cutoff.
Negative CT pulmonary angiography.

do_not_rely.text: D-dimer when clinical probability is high.
A normal chest radiograph.
The standard Wells route in unstable or pregnant patients.

ad.validation: ESC 2024 recommends an ADD-RS-based diagnostic algorithm (class I, level B); MDCalc notes ADD-RS plus D-dimer lacks external validation.

eliminate_when.text: ADD-RS 1 or less and D-dimer below 500 ng/mL (FEU): consider stopping the work-up.
In ADvISED this strategy missed about 0.3% of acute aortic syndromes.
In the later PROFUNDUS study, ADD-RS 1 or less with negative D-dimer had a 0.2% failure rate.
Negative ECG-gated contrast CT, the first-line imaging in ESC 2024 (class I, level C).

do_not_rely.text: D-dimer alone.
ADD-RS of 0 as proof.
Chest radiography.
A D-dimer threshold in the wrong units (assumes FEU).

eliminate_when.text: Normal chest radiograph with respiratory distress, pleuritic pain and hypoxia.

do_not_rely.text: Exam findings alone.

eliminate_when.text: Normal chest radiograph makes it unlikely, not impossible.

do_not_rely.text: Exam findings alone.

pc.validation: Diagnostic criteria only; no exclusion rule found.

do_not_rely.text: A normal ECG: without ST elevation the diagnosis is easily missed.
Chest film, markers or troponin as diagnostic; only ECG and echo help establish it.

pc.no_rule_note: No formal exclusion rule found. Diagnosis needs at least two of four criteria.

do_not_rely.text: Chest wall tenderness alone.

nc.no_rule_note: Not eliminated; it is what remains.

gaps.title: Local resources
gaps.text: Some sites cannot run acute troponin, so the pathway cannot be applied as written.

gaps.title: Which PE score
gaps.text: Wells, revised Geneva and YEARS lead to the same next steps, but protocols differ.

gaps.title: US versus Europe on dissection
gaps.text: ESC 2024 sends ADD-RS 2 or more to CT regardless of D-dimer; AHA guidance lacks consensus on the ADD-RS cut-off and on D-dimer.

gaps.title: Parallel hypotheses
gaps.text: No source found on prioritizing ACS, PE and dissection work-ups run at the same time.

situations.title: Acute shortness of breath
situations.priority: Among the top ED reasons for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.

layer0.label: Complaint
layer0.detail: New or worsening breathlessness.

layer0.label: History
layer0.detail: Known heart failure, lung disease, VTE risk factors.

layer0.label: Exam
layer0.detail: Pain on inspiration and one-sided absent breath sounds point to pneumothorax; fever, localized pleuritic pain and dullness point to pneumonia.

layer0.label: First tests
layer0.detail: ECG, chest radiograph, natriuretic peptide.

gate.label: Respiratory failure or instability
gate.detail: Resuscitate first; the elimination route assumes a stabilized patient.

gate.label: Stable
gate.detail: Work through heart, lung and clot causes in parallel.

situations.gate_note: Gate wording is a structural convention, not taken from a source.

hypotheses.name: Pneumothorax
hypotheses.clue: Pain on inspiration, absent breath sounds

steps.title: History and exam
steps.description: Sets which causes are plausible.

ptx.text: Dyspnea, pain on inspiration, one-sided absent breath sounds.

pna.text: Fever, localized pleuritic pain, dullness, egophony.

acs.text: Shortness of breath counts as an anginal equivalent.

steps.title: 12-lead ECG
steps.description: Screens for ischemia.

acs.text: Ischemic change escalates; one normal ECG does not rule ACS out.

steps.title: Chest radiograph
steps.description: Finds lung causes and changes PE probability.

ptx.text: Normal film with distress, pleuritic pain and hypoxia excludes pneumothorax.

pna.text: Infiltrate confirms; a normal film makes pneumonia unlikely.

pe.text: A normal film in a hypoxic, distressed patient raises PE probability.

ahf.text: With echocardiography and judgment, helps in the natriuretic peptide grey zone.

steps.title: Natriuretic peptide
steps.timing: Single measurement in new suspected heart failure
steps.description: Rule-out test for heart failure.

ahf.text: BNP below 100 ng/L or NT-proBNP below 300 ng/L rules out heart failure.

steps.title: PE route
steps.timing: In parallel if PE is open
steps.description: Wells or PERC, then D-dimer or CTPA (see chest pain).

pe.text: Low pre-test probability with negative D-dimer, or negative CTPA.

steps.title: Echocardiography
steps.timing: If heart failure is not ruled out
steps.description: Confirms the cardiac abnormality.

eliminate_when.text: BNP below 100 ng/L or NT-proBNP below 300 ng/L in new suspected acute heart failure.

do_not_rely.text: The rule-out threshold in older patients, obesity or prior heart failure: false negatives of 1 in 10 to 1 in 5.
NT-proBNP rule-out above age 75: negative predictive value fell to about 88% in one cohort.

eliminate_when.text: Low pre-test probability and negative D-dimer.
Negative CTPA.

do_not_rely.text: D-dimer when probability is high.

eliminate_when.text: Low-risk class with non-ischemic ECG and negative serial troponin.

do_not_rely.text: One normal ECG.

eliminate_when.text: Normal chest radiograph with distress, pleuritic pain and hypoxia.

do_not_rely.text: Exam alone.

eliminate_when.text: Normal chest radiograph makes it unlikely.

do_not_rely.text: Exam alone.

copd.no_rule_note: No route sourced; GOLD and GINA guidance would be the next sources.

gaps.title: Grey zone
gaps.text: Between rule-out and rule-in natriuretic peptide thresholds, about half of older patients have heart failure; echo and judgment decide.

gaps.title: Unsourced gate
gaps.text: The stabilization gate and the COPD/asthma branch need sourcing.

situations.title: Acute lower abdominal or pelvic pain
situations.population: Adults, including women of reproductive age
situations.priority: Abdominal pain is the leading ED reason for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.

layer0.label: Complaint
layer0.detail: Pain in the lower abdomen or pelvis; its location narrows the list.

layer0.label: Pregnancy status
layer0.detail: Urine or serum beta-hCG is the first step in women who could be pregnant.

layer0.label: Exam clues
layer0.detail: Migration from the umbilicus to the right lower quadrant suggests appendicitis; left lower quadrant tenderness suggests diverticulitis.

layer0.label: Patient group
layer0.detail: Adult, child or pregnant; this changes which imaging comes first.

gate.label: Positive pregnancy test with pain
gate.detail: Ectopic pregnancy must be considered; ultrasound first.

gate.label: Not pregnant
gate.detail: Choose imaging by suspected source: gynecologic or not.

situations.gate_note: Urgent causes to consider first in women of reproductive age include ectopic pregnancy, ruptured ovarian cyst, ovarian torsion, appendicitis and pelvic inflammatory disease.

hypotheses.name: Appendicitis
hypotheses.clue: Pain migrating to the right lower quadrant

hypotheses.name: Ovarian cyst or pelvic inflammatory disease
Ureteral stone
hypotheses.clue: Flank pain radiating; see flank pain

steps.title: History and exam
steps.description: Location and migration of pain narrow the list.

appy.text: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant.

torsion.text: Right- or left-sided pelvic pain keeps torsion on the list.

stone.text: Right-sided pelvic pain can also be a stone.

steps.title: Pregnancy test
steps.timing: Before imaging, in anyone who could be pregnant
steps.description: Decides whether pregnancy causes are possible and which imaging is safe.

ectopic.text: A negative serum beta-hCG essentially excludes acute ectopic pregnancy.

steps.title: Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler
steps.description: Transabdominal plus transvaginal ultrasound is the usual first imaging.

ectopic.text: First-line imaging when hCG is positive.

torsion.text: Ultrasound with Doppler is the initial study for gynecologic causes.

gyn.text: Characterizes cysts and complications of pelvic inflammatory disease.

appy.text: First choice in children and pregnancy; often inconclusive in pregnancy, then MRI.

steps.title: Contrast CT
steps.timing: Nonpregnant adults with a suspected non-gynecologic cause
steps.description: Most accurate test for appendicitis and other bowel causes.

appy.text: CT is the most accurate study for appendicitis and its alternatives.

divert.text: CT with IV contrast is best for gastrointestinal causes such as diverticulitis.

evidence.text: Cochrane review: at 43% prevalence, a positive CT means about a 92% chance of appendicitis and a negative CT about 4%.

eliminate_when.text: Negative serum beta-hCG.

appy.validation: ACR criteria for test choice; Cochrane diagnostic review for accuracy.

eliminate_when.text: Negative CT in an adult: at a 43% prevalence the probability of appendicitis falls to about 4% (Cochrane review). A strong reduction, not certainty.

do_not_rely.text: A single inconclusive ultrasound in pregnancy; most are inconclusive, so MRI follows.

torsion.no_rule_note: No explicit exclusion rule extracted; ultrasound with Doppler is the first study.

stone.no_rule_note: Route lives in the flank pain situation.

gaps.title: Upper abdominal pain
gaps.text: Right upper quadrant and epigastric pain are not covered; ultrasound is the usual first test for right upper quadrant pain.

gaps.title: Operator dependence
gaps.text: Ultrasound performance depends on operator training.

gaps.title: Clinical scores
gaps.text: Scores such as Alvarado were not sourced in this pass.

situations.title: Acute nontraumatic headache
situations.priority: Among the top five ED reasons for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.

layer0.label: Complaint
layer0.detail: New or different headache; how fast it reached peak intensity (peak within 1 hour matters for the SAH rule).

layer0.label: History: red flags
layer0.detail: SNNOOP10: systemic symptoms including fever, cancer history, neurologic deficit, sudden onset, onset after 65, new or changed pattern, positional, triggered by cough or exertion, papilledema, progressive, pregnancy, painful eye with autonomic features, trauma, immune compromise, painkiller overuse or new drug.

layer0.label: Exam
layer0.detail: Full neurologic exam, level of consciousness, neck pain or stiffness, limited neck flexion, papilledema, fever.

gate.label: Neurologic deficit or decreased consciousness
gate.detail: A red flag for a secondary cause; the ACEP rule-out tools below do not apply because they assume a normal neurologic exam.

gate.label: Alert, normal neurologic exam
gate.detail: Screen red flags, then apply the SAH rule if the headache peaked within 1 hour.

situations.gate_note: Most headaches are primary, but secondary causes must be screened for first.

steps.title: Red-flag history (SNNOOP10)
steps.description: Structured screen of every new or different headache.

sah.text: Sudden or thunderclap onset is a red flag.

men.text: Fever and systemic symptoms are a red flag.

sec.text: Each flag raises suspicion, but specificity is not validated.

prim.text: With no red flags, primary headache becomes more likely.

steps.title: Neurologic exam
steps.description: Decides which rules can be used.

sah.text: Neck stiffness is strongly associated, but no single sign rules SAH out.

men.text: Abnormal consciousness or focal deficit means CT before lumbar puncture.

sec.text: A deficit or papilledema is a red flag.

steps.title: Ottawa SAH rule
steps.timing: Alert patients, normal neuro exam, peak within 1 hour
steps.description: Six features: age 40 or older, neck pain or stiffness, witnessed loss of consciousness, onset with exertion, thunderclap onset, limited neck flexion.

sah.text: None present: high sensitivity supports ruling SAH out; any present only means investigate (low specificity).

steps.title: Noncontrast head CT
steps.description: First imaging test for suspected SAH and before LP in at-risk patients.

sah.text: Normal CT within 6 hours of onset, with normal neuro exam, rules out nontraumatic SAH.

men.text: Only needed before LP if immunocompromised, CNS disease, new seizure, papilledema, abnormal consciousness or focal deficit.

steps.title: Lumbar puncture or CT angiography
steps.timing: If still at risk after a negative CT
steps.description: Second-line test chosen with the patient.

sah.text: LP or CTA safely rules out SAH in a patient still at risk after a negative CT.

men.text: Diagnosis depends on CSF examination; blood cultures and LP should be done promptly.

steps.title: If no red flags and secondary causes are excluded
steps.description: Primary headache becomes the working diagnosis.

prim.text: Diagnosis of exclusion once red flags are absent or answered.

eliminate_when.text: Ottawa SAH rule negative in an alert patient with normal neuro exam and peak within 1 hour.
Normal noncontrast CT within 6 hours of onset with normal neuro exam.
Negative LP or CTA after a negative CT in a patient still at risk.

do_not_rely.text: A single sign or symptom.
The Ottawa rule outside its population (abnormal neuro exam, slower peak).
A positive Ottawa rule as proof; it has low specificity.

men.validation: IDSA 2004 via secondary summaries; check for newer guidance.

do_not_rely.text: Delaying antibiotics for CT; cultures and antibiotics come first when CT is needed.
A normal head CT as proof that LP is safe in every patient.

men.no_rule_note: No formal exclusion rule sourced; diagnosis depends on CSF examination.

sec.validation: Red flags from a narrative review.

do_not_rely.text: Imaging everyone; many scans find nothing relevant.

sec.no_rule_note: No single elimination rule; each secondary cause needs its own route.

prim.no_rule_note: Not eliminated; it is what remains when red flags are absent.

gaps.title: Rule validation
gaps.text: Early reviews noted the Ottawa SAH rule had mainly Canadian validation; check local validity.

gaps.title: CT/LP versus CT/CTA
gaps.text: ACEP recommends shared decision making between the two second-line strategies.

gaps.title: Red-flag evidence
gaps.text: Most red flags lack prospective data on specificity.

situations.title: Fever in an adult (suspected sepsis)
situations.priority: Fever is among the top ED reasons for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.

layer0.label: Signs of infection and vital signs
layer0.detail: Screened with NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS or SIRS rather than qSOFA alone.

layer0.label: Sepsis certainty
layer0.detail: The 2026 guideline grades suspected sepsis as definite, probable, possible or unlikely.

gate.label: Probable or definite sepsis, or shock
gate.detail: Treat as an emergency: antimicrobials within 1 hour of recognition.

gate.label: Possible sepsis without shock
gate.detail: Time-limited investigation; if infection is likely, antimicrobials within 3 hours.

situations.gate_note: Updated to the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline, which replaced the 2021 edition.

steps.title: Screening tool
steps.description: NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS or SIRS rather than qSOFA alone (strong recommendation).

sepsis.text: A negative qSOFA alone does not rule sepsis out.

steps.title: Grade the certainty
steps.description: Definite, probable, possible or unlikely sepsis, using the guideline's standard language.

sepsis.text: Sets urgency: 1 hour for probable or definite, a time-limited work-up for possible.

steps.title: Time-limited investigation
steps.description: Search for infection within a set time before committing to antimicrobials.

sepsis.text: If infection becomes likely, antimicrobials within 3 hours; the guideline does not state a formal exclusion test.

noninf.text: The 2026 guideline addresses noninfectious causes in possible sepsis without shock; details not extracted.

steps.title: Blood lactate
steps.description: Suggested in the 2021 edition; re-check against 2026.

sepsis.text: Elevated lactate supports sepsis and guides resuscitation (2021 statement).

steps.title: Source search
steps.description: Chest film; lumbar puncture when meningitis is suspected.

men.text: CSF examination is the diagnostic test.

sepsis.validation: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 (lactate and procalcitonin statements still from 2021).

do_not_rely.text: A negative qSOFA alone.
Procalcitonin to decide whether to start antimicrobials (2021 statement; re-check).

sepsis.no_rule_note: No formal exclusion test. The 2026 guideline grades certainty and uses a time-limited investigation for possible sepsis.

do_not_rely.text: Delaying antibiotics for CT.

eliminate_when.text: Normal chest radiograph makes it unlikely.

noninf.no_rule_note: Named in the 2026 guideline; statements not extracted.

gaps.title: 2021 leftovers
gaps.text: Lactate and procalcitonin steps still cite the 2021 edition and need checking against 2026.

gaps.title: Children
gaps.text: The 2026 pediatric Surviving Sepsis guideline is separate and not included.

situations.title: Syncope (transient loss of consciousness)
situations.priority: Common ED presentation with its own US and European guidelines.

layer0.label: The event
layer0.detail: Prodrome, position (standing, sitting, supine), exertion, palpitations, triggers such as pain, cough, micturition or prolonged standing.

layer0.label: History
layer0.detail: Structural heart disease or prior myocardial infarction, family history of sudden cardiac death at a young age.

layer0.label: Exam
layer0.detail: Physical examination including lying and standing blood pressure.

layer0.label: 12-lead ECG
layer0.detail: Useful in the initial evaluation (class I).

gate.label: Any high-risk feature
gate.detail: New chest discomfort, breathlessness, abdominal pain or headache; syncope during exertion or supine; palpitations right before syncope; structural heart disease. Evaluate in hospital or with ECG monitoring.

gate.label: Low-risk features only
gate.detail: Typical reflex prodrome or trigger, or syncope on standing up. Likely reflex or orthostatic; discharge can be considered.

situations.gate_note: Not all high-risk patients need admission; risk scores may be reasonable but are not better than clinical judgment.

hypotheses.name: Cardiac (arrhythmic or structural) syncope
hypotheses.clue: Exertional or supine, palpitations, heart disease

hypotheses.name: Serious condition presenting as syncope
hypotheses.clue: New chest pain, breathlessness, abdominal pain or headache

steps.title: Event history
steps.description: Separates low-risk reflex patterns from high-risk features.

card.text: Exertion, supine position, sudden palpitations, or no or very short prodrome with heart disease.

serious.text: New chest discomfort, breathlessness, abdominal pain or headache is a major high-risk feature.

orth.text: Syncope on standing up from lying or sitting.

reflex.text: Prodrome of light-headedness, warmth, sweating or nausea; pain, crowded hot places, cough or micturition triggers.

steps.title: Exam with lying and standing blood pressure
steps.description: Part of the standard initial evaluation.

orth.text: Lying and standing BP is the bedside test for orthostatic causes.

card.text: Findings of structural heart disease are high risk.

steps.title: 12-lead ECG
steps.description: Class I in the initial evaluation.

card.text: An abnormal ECG turns minor features into high-risk ones.

steps.title: Risk stratification and disposition
steps.description: Sorts patients into high, intermediate and low risk.

card.text: Low-risk features only: discharge from the ED is recommended for patients without recurrence.

reflex.text: Low-risk patients mostly have reflex syncope with a good prognosis.

steps.title: Targeted tests only when suspected
steps.description: Routine labs, cardiac imaging and carotid imaging are not useful without a specific reason.

card.text: ECG monitoring in high-risk patients with suspected arrhythmia; cardiac imaging only if a cardiac cause is suspected.

reflex.text: Tilt testing when reflex syncope is suspected.

orth.text: Tilt testing when an orthostatic cause is suspected.

eliminate_when.text: Only low-risk features after history, exam and ECG: ESC 2018 recommends discharge from the ED (class I, level B). Treating this disposition as elimination is the inferred part.

do_not_rely.text: Routine comprehensive laboratory testing.
Routine cardiac imaging without a suspected cardiac cause.
Risk scores as better than clinical judgment.

serious.no_rule_note: Route depends on the underlying condition (for example PE or dissection); see the chest pain situation.

do_not_rely.text: Carotid imaging without focal neurologic findings.

orth.no_rule_note: No elimination threshold extracted; orthostatic criteria are in the ESC guideline.

reflex.no_rule_note: Diagnosis is clinical; tilt testing when suspected.

gaps.title: Two guidelines
gaps.text: US (2017) and European (2018) guidelines overlap but differ in detail.

gaps.title: Intermediate risk
gaps.text: Patients with neither high- nor low-risk features have no single sourced pathway here.

gaps.title: Orthostatic thresholds
gaps.text: Exact blood pressure criteria were not extracted in this pass.

situations.title: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding
situations.priority: GI bleeding causes more than half a million US admissions a year.

layer0.label: Complaint
layer0.detail: Vomiting red blood or coffee-ground material, or black stools; bleeding from esophagus, stomach or duodenum.

layer0.label: Vitals and labs
layer0.detail: Inputs for the Glasgow-Blatchford score.

gate.label: Not very low risk
gate.detail: Hospital care; endoscopy within 24 hours.

gate.label: Very low risk (Glasgow-Blatchford 0 to 1)
gate.detail: Outpatient follow-up rather than admission, if no other reason to stay.

situations.gate_note: This situation is mostly risk triage; the cause is found at endoscopy rather than eliminated step by step.

hypotheses.name: Other upper GI source (varices, tears, others)

steps.title: Risk score
steps.description: Glasgow-Blatchford score.

needs_intervention.text: Score 0 to 1 identifies very-low-risk patients; the score is about 99% sensitive for need for intervention.

steps.title: Endoscopy
steps.description: Finds and treats the source.

ulcer.text: Endoscopic therapy for ulcers with active bleeding or a visible vessel.

other_ugi.text: Endoscopy identifies the source (non-ulcer routes not sourced).

needs_intervention.validation: ACG 2021, conditional recommendation, very low quality evidence.

eliminate_when.text: Glasgow-Blatchford score 0 to 1 with no other reason for admission.

do_not_rely.text: The score without considering age, comorbidities and follow-up reliability.

gaps.title: Lower GI bleeding
gaps.text: Lower GI bleeding has a separate ACG guideline, not included.

situations.title: Unilateral leg swelling or pain (suspected DVT)
situations.priority: High-volume VTE presentation with a GRADE guideline.

layer0.label: Complaint
layer0.detail: One-sided leg swelling or pain.

layer0.label: History
layer0.detail: Prior DVT or PE, cancer, recent immobilization; whether another diagnosis is as likely.

gate.label: Breathlessness or chest pain
gate.detail: Treat as suspected PE and use that route.

gate.label: Leg symptoms only
gate.detail: Estimate pre-test probability, then test.

situations.gate_note: Diagnostic strategy depends on the estimated pre-test probability.

steps.title: Pre-test probability (Wells for DVT)
steps.description: Low, intermediate or high; DVT prevalence about 10% or less, 25% and 50% or more.

alt.text: An alternative diagnosis being as likely lowers the score.

steps.title: Highly sensitive D-dimer
steps.description: Rule-out test.

dvt.text: Negative D-dimer at low pre-test probability: no further testing.

steps.title: Compression ultrasound
steps.description: Proximal or whole-leg ultrasound.

dvt.text: Positive scan confirms; a negative whole-leg scan or negative serial proximal scans end the work-up.

eliminate_when.text: Low pre-test probability and negative highly sensitive D-dimer.
Negative whole-leg ultrasound, negative serial proximal ultrasound, or negative D-dimer after a negative proximal scan: no further testing.
ASH 2018: at intermediate or high probability, proximal or whole-limb ultrasound first, with a one-week repeat after a negative scan in higher-prevalence groups.

do_not_rely.text: D-dimer as the first test at high probability; imaging is warranted.
A single negative proximal scan when the D-dimer is positive; repeat at one week or scan the whole leg.

alt.no_rule_note: Specific alternatives (cellulitis, ruptured Baker cyst) not sourced.

gaps.title: Score cut-offs
gaps.text: Exact Wells DVT cut-offs differ between versions; prevalence bands are used instead.

gaps.title: Distal DVT
gaps.text: The clinical relevance of calf-vein clots found on ultrasound is uncertain.

situations.title: Acute dizziness or vertigo
situations.priority: Common ED complaint with a 2023 GRADE guideline.

layer0.label: Timing and triggers
layer0.detail: Continuous for more than 24 hours (acute vestibular syndrome), triggered by position, or spontaneous episodes.

layer0.label: Exam
layer0.detail: Nystagmus, HINTS (head impulse, nystagmus, test of skew), gait, Dix-Hallpike when positional.

gate.label: Continuous dizziness (acute vestibular syndrome)
gate.detail: Stroke must be excluded with HINTS by a trained examiner, then MRI if central or equivocal.

gate.label: Positional (triggered) episodes
gate.detail: Dix-Hallpike for posterior canal BPPV; no CT and no routine MRI.

situations.gate_note: Untrained clinicians apply and interpret HINTS inaccurately; GRACE-3 recommends training.

steps.title: Classify by timing and triggers
steps.description: Decides which bedside test applies.

steps.title: Dix-Hallpike test
steps.description: Diagnoses posterior canal BPPV.

bppv.text: Positive test diagnoses posterior canal BPPV; treat with Epley maneuver.

steps.title: HINTS exam by a trained clinician
steps.description: Separates central from peripheral patterns.

stroke.text: A peripheral HINTS pattern helps rule out stroke, but only when performed by trained clinicians.

periph.text: Peripheral pattern supports a peripheral cause.

steps.title: MRI
steps.description: Confirmatory test.

stroke.text: MRI confirms; in the first 48 hours it misses about 1 in 5 strokes presenting as dizziness.

eliminate_when.text: Peripheral HINTS pattern in a patient with true acute vestibular syndrome, examined by a trained clinician.

do_not_rely.text: HINTS done by untrained clinicians or in the wrong patients.
An early negative MRI alone: about 80% sensitive in the first 48 hours.
CT for positional dizziness.

bppv.no_rule_note: Confirmed rather than eliminated; positive Dix-Hallpike.

periph.no_rule_note: Supported by a peripheral HINTS pattern.

gaps.title: Training
gaps.text: HINTS accuracy depends on examiner training, which most emergency physicians lack.

situations.title: Acute focal neurologic deficit (suspected stroke)
situations.population: Adults (the 2026 guideline also adds pediatric guidance, not encoded here)

layer0.label: Complaint
layer0.detail: Sudden weakness, numbness, speech or vision loss.

layer0.label: Timing
layer0.detail: Time last known well decides treatment eligibility.

layer0.label: Bedside glucose
layer0.detail: Checked before thrombolysis; severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia can mimic stroke.

gate.label: Within a treatment window
gate.detail: Stroke pathway immediately; brain imaging within 25 minutes; other tests must not delay reperfusion.

gate.label: Outside known windows
gate.detail: Still image urgently; the 2026 guideline widens some windows with perfusion imaging.

situations.gate_note: Verified against the 2026 AHA/ASA guideline, which replaced the 2018 guideline and 2019 update.

steps.title: Bedside glucose
steps.description: Detects and urgently corrects severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia.

hypo.text: Normal glucose, or a disabling deficit that persists after correction, means glucose does not explain the deficit.

steps.title: Brain imaging: noncontrast CT or MRI
steps.description: Assesses ischemic burden and excludes hemorrhage before any reperfusion treatment (class 1, level A).

ich.text: Imaging without hemorrhage excludes intracranial hemorrhage before reperfusion.

ais.text: Mild to moderate early ischemic change neither precludes nor delays thrombolysis.

steps.title: ECG and troponin
steps.description: Recommended, but must not delay treatment.

ais.text: Baseline ECG and troponin must not delay IV thrombolysis or thrombectomy.

steps.title: Vascular and perfusion imaging
steps.timing: Suspected large vessel occlusion within 24 hours; extended windows
steps.description: CT/CTA or MRI/MRA as fast as possible for thrombectomy selection.

ais.text: Perfusion imaging can select some unknown-onset patients for thrombolysis up to 9 hours.

eliminate_when.text: Normal bedside glucose.
A disabling deficit persisting after glucose correction; thrombolysis is still recommended then.
Noncontrast CT or MRI without hemorrhage.

do_not_rely.text: Delaying treatment for ECG, troponin or advanced imaging.
Mild early ischemic change on CT as a reason to withhold thrombolysis.

ais.no_rule_note: Stroke is confirmed or treated, not eliminated, in this route.

mimic.no_rule_note: Seizure, migraine and other mimics not sourced.

gaps.title: Pediatric stroke
gaps.text: The 2026 guideline adds pediatric recommendations, not encoded here.

gaps.title: Other mimics
gaps.text: Mimics other than glucose disorders are not sourced.

situations.title: Acute low back pain
situations.priority: Leading cause of disability under age 45; imaging overuse is a known problem.

layer0.label: Duration
layer0.detail: Acute means 6 weeks or less.

layer0.label: Red flags
layer0.detail: New urinary retention or overflow incontinence, loss of anal tone or fecal incontinence, saddle anesthesia, progressive leg weakness; also cancer history, infection, fracture risk.

gate.label: Cauda equina features or severe or progressive deficit
gate.detail: MRI urgently.

gate.label: No red flags
gate.detail: No imaging for uncomplicated pain under 6 weeks.

situations.gate_note: Most uncomplicated acute low back pain needs no imaging.

steps.title: Red-flag history and exam
steps.description: The cornerstone of initial assessment.

ces.text: Bladder, bowel or saddle symptoms, or progressive weakness.

mech.text: No red flags makes uncomplicated pain likely.

steps.title: No imaging if no red flags
steps.description: All imaging is rated usually not appropriate.

mech.text: Half of patients recover in 2 weeks and 90% by 3 months.

steps.title: MRI
steps.timing: Red flags, or no improvement after 6 weeks
steps.description: Modality of choice for most patients who need imaging.

ces.text: MRI evaluates the cauda equina better than CT.

malig.text: MRI is preferred when malignancy is suspected.

infx.text: MRI is the modality of choice for most patients who need imaging.

do_not_rely.text: Imaging every patient; it does not improve outcomes in uncomplicated pain.

ces.no_rule_note: No red flags means it is not pursued; MRI decides when flags are present.

do_not_rely.text: Malignancy red flags as proven; most lack empirical support.

malig.no_rule_note: No exclusion rule beyond absent red flags.

infx.no_rule_note: No exclusion rule beyond absent red flags.

fx.no_rule_note: No exclusion rule beyond absent red flags.

mech.no_rule_note: What remains when red flags are absent.

gaps.title: Red-flag evidence
gaps.text: Many red flags lack empirical support; validated thresholds are missing.

situations.title: Acute flank pain (suspected stone)
situations.priority: Has a dedicated ACR topic with four variants.

layer0.label: Complaint
layer0.detail: Sudden, colicky flank pain, often with blood in the urine.

layer0.label: History
layer0.detail: Known stones, pregnancy, signs of infection.

gate.label: Signs of infection
gate.detail: Covered by the separate ACR acute pyelonephritis topic.

gate.label: No infection signs
gate.detail: Image by patient group.

hypotheses.name: Other abdominal cause (appendicitis, diverticulitis, ovarian torsion)

steps.title: Noncontrast CT
steps.description: Imaging study of choice.

stone.text: Reliably shows stone size, position and complications.

alt_abd.text: Also diagnoses other causes of abdominal pain.

evidence.text: In one prospective comparison, CT found an alternative diagnosis in about a third of patients.
For causes other than stones, noncontrast CT and ultrasound had similar accuracy (CT sensitivity 74%).

steps.title: Ultrasound
steps.timing: Pregnancy, or to look for obstruction
steps.description: First choice in pregnancy; less sensitive for stones.

stone.text: Shows obstruction; MRI may follow in pregnancy.

steps.title: Contrast CT or MRI
steps.description: Second-line imaging.

stone.text: CT urogram or MRI may be appropriate.

stone.validation: ACR criteria for test choice; meta-analysis data for accuracy.

eliminate_when.text: No stone or secondary signs on noncontrast CT: pooled sensitivity 94 to 100% in a meta-analysis.
Low-dose CT performs similarly (negative likelihood ratio about 0.04) for stones of 2 to 3 mm or more.

do_not_rely.text: Ultrasound alone to exclude a stone; it is less sensitive.

pyelo.no_rule_note: Separate ACR pyelonephritis topic not sourced.

do_not_rely.text: A stone-protocol CT as proof that nothing else is wrong; one study found 74% sensitivity for alternative causes.

alt_abd.no_rule_note: No reliable exclusion rule; noncontrast CT missed about a quarter of alternative causes in one study.

gaps.title: Vascular causes
gaps.text: Aortic aneurysm as a flank pain mimic was not sourced.
